objective: Sub-goal B198 (MEET-TWIST-20261118-001's selected direction; coordinator's go-ahead, 18 November 2026): presentations of one line differ only in how their knots nest, which the line's states and disagreement counts do not show. After k new distinctions of KF3, how much of the nesting does a grown base's table of disagreement counts reveal, in law and per sample, and from which k does it determine the bare bracketing? Serves G16; tests A97 directly (distance as the only form of information).
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending): the knots' nesting is a distance only in part and only after growth. Before growth every presentation of a line has the same disagreement counts; one KF3-grown base's counts carry at most about two thirds of the information about the bare bracketing (0.63, 0.65, 0.62 at five to seven, peaking near n0 - 4 new distinctions, then falling), less than revealing the knots directly; the counts determine the states here, so the rest is lost, not hidden; fill-point distances measure steps along the line, not the nesting. 4 of 5 predictions held.
